desc:
The tilt of a node is the absolute difference between the sum of all values in its left subtree and the sum of all values in its right subtree. A missing subtree counts as a sum of 0. The node's own value is not part of its tilt.

Return the sum of the tilts of all nodes of the tree.

How trees are given. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order (top to bottom, left to right). The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn; a missing child is written as -1 (real node values are never negative). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped.

For example, [1,2,3,-1,4] is the tree whose root 1 has children 2 and 3; node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child; node 3 is a leaf.

Example 1

tree = [1,2,3]
Output: 1
The root has tilt |2 - 3| = 1; both leaves have tilt 0.

Example 2

tree = [4,2,9,3,5,-1,7]
Output: 15
Node 2 has tilt |3 - 5| = 2, node 9 has tilt |0 - 7| = 7, the root has tilt |10 - 16| = 6, the leaves have tilt 0.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly
hints: To know a node's tilt you need the total value of each child subtree. Computing each of those from scratch for every node is slow on tall trees.
Compute subtree sums bottom-up: the sum of a subtree is the node's value plus the sums of its two child subtrees. While you do that, the two child sums are exactly the numbers the tilt needs.
In the level-order numbering every child has a larger index than its parent, so looping over nodes from the last index to the first processes children before parents without recursion.
editorial: Define S(u) as the sum of all values in the subtree of u. Then S(u) = val[u] + S(left) + S(right) and the tilt of u is |S(left) - S(right)|. A single bottom-up pass computes both at every node, so each node is touched once.

Recomputing the subtree sums separately for every node costs O(n) per node, O(n<sup>2</sup>) on a chain. The bottom-up pass is O(n) time and O(n) memory (O(h) with recursion). The answer is at most about 4.5 * 10<sup>8</sup> here, so it fits in 32 bits.
solution:
def parse(tree):
    val, left, right = [tree[0]], [-1], [-1]
    i, u = 1, 0
    while u < len(val) and i < len(tree):
        for kids in (left, right):
            if i < len(tree):
                x = tree[i]
                i += 1
                if x != -1:
                    kids[u] = len(val)
                    val.append(x)
                    left.append(-1)
                    right.append(-1)
        u += 1
    return val, left, right


def treeTilt(tree):
    val, left, right = parse(tree)
    n = len(val)
    s = val[:]
    total = 0
    for u in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        a = s[left[u]] if left[u] != -1 else 0
        b = s[right[u]] if right[u] != -1 else 0
        total += abs(a - b)
        s[u] = val[u] + a + b
    return total
